property_summary: SetMinSum can only be called successfully before Initialized() is called (i.e., calling SetMinSum after Initialized() reverts).

Calling SetMinSum(x) on the correct contract never updates MinSum when the contract is already initialized (i.e., if Initialized() was called, subsequent SetMinSum calls revert and leave MinSum unchanged), whereas the mutant that assigns MinSum before the initialized check can cause MinSum to appear changed for some inputs where the call reverts from the caller's perspective.

For any caller and value, if SetMinSum completes (does not revert) then C.MinSum equals the provided value; the mutant that writes MinSum before checking `intitalized` can make MinSum appear updated despite the call reverting from the caller's perspective in some interposed external call scenarios, violating the invariant that successful calls set MinSum and reverted calls never leave observable state changes.

For any caller and value, if SetMinSum call reverts (ok==false) then MinSum remains equal to its prior value in the reference; the mutant that writes MinSum before the initialized check can make MinSum change even though the external call reverted (when the contract's Initialized flag causes a revert), so there exists inputs where ok==false but MinSum changed — the test detects that by checking MinSum didn't change when the call reverts.

For any caller and value, calling SetMinSum either completes successfully and sets MinSum to the provided value, or it reverts and leaves MinSum equal to its previous value; the mutant that assigns MinSum before checking `intitalized` can cause MinSum to be set even when the external caller observes a revert in some call sequences, violating that invariant.

For any caller and value, attempting SetMinSum either reverts (ok==false) and leaves MinSum unchanged, or succeeds (ok==true) and sets MinSum to the provided value; the mutant that writes MinSum before checking `intitalized` can make MinSum observable as changed even when the call to SetMinSum reverts in certain call contexts, breaking this rule.

After calling SetLogFile(x) on an uninitialized contract, the public LogFile getter must return x (the reference assigns it; the mutant that omits assignment will leave LogFile unchanged and thus violate this for some x).

For any address input, calling SetLogFile(addr) on a fresh (uninitialized) contract sets the public LogFile to that address; the mutant that omits the assignment will break this for some address inputs.

For any nonzero address A, calling SetLogFile(A) on a freshly deployed, not-yet-initialized contract sets C.LogFile() to A; the mutant that removes the assignment leaves LogFile unchanged for some A, violating this rule.

For any address X, if C has its LogFile initially zero and you call SetLogFile(X) before Initialized() is called, then after the call the public LogFile getter equals X; the mutant that omits the assignment can leave LogFile unchanged for some X and thus violates this property.

For any address L and caller A, if C has been deployed fresh and SetLogFile(L) is invoked by A before Initialized(), then the reference contract's public LogFile getter will reflect L after the call; the mutant that omits the assignment can leave LogFile unchanged for some L so that the getter does not equal L (the test fuzzes both caller and L to find such a case).

For any provided _log address, calling SetLogFile on the correct contract makes LogFile point to that address (i.e. c.LogFile() == _log), whereas the mutant that always stores address(0) will break this for any non-zero _log (so there exists inputs where c.LogFile() != address(0)).

For any provided non-zero log-address, the correct contract stores that address in LogFile when SetLogFile is called before initialization; the mutant instead always stores address(0), so there exist inputs (non-zero addresses) where the stored LogFile differs.

For every address _log and before initialization, calling SetLogFile(_log) results in c.LogFile() equal to the provided _log; the mutant instead sets LogFile to address(0) and thus for some non-zero _log this property is violated.

For every non-initialized C and for every address A, calling SetLogFile(A) leaves the contract's public LogFile getter equal to A; the mutant that always assigns address(0) will violate this for some A (any non-zero address), so there exist fuzzed inputs that make the getter differ.

For any caller and any address _log, if SetLogFile(_log) is called before Initialized(), the contract's public LogFile getter must equal the provided _log; the mutant that writes address(0) breaks this by making the getter differ for some _log inputs (any non-zero address).

For any caller address X and any supplied _log address L, after SetLogFile(L) completes the contract's LogFile getter equals L (the reference stores the provided address); the mutant that stores msg.sender instead will violate this for inputs where msg.sender != L (which the fuzzer can find).

For any caller and provided address _log, the reference stores LogFile == _log after SetLogFile(_log) returns; the mutant stores msg.sender instead, so when caller != _log the mutant breaks this rule.

For all callers and provided addresses _log, after SetLogFile(_log) returns the contract's LogFile getter equals the provided address _log (the reference stores the provided address; the mutant stores msg.sender and thus violates this whenever caller != _log).

For every caller addr A and provided address L, after SetMinSum and SetLogFile are called before Initialized, the contract's LogFile getter equals the provided address L; the mutant that stores msg.sender instead will violate this whenever A != L (fuzzer can find such pair).

For every caller A and provided address L, after calling SetLogFile(L) (before Initialized) the contract's public LogFile getter returns L (the reference stores the provided address; the mutant stores msg.sender and thus will differ whenever A != L).

For any caller and any nonzero added lock delta, the reference sets holder.unlockTime to max(oldUnlockTime, block.timestamp + _lockTime) (i.e. new unlockTime is >= oldUnlockTime and at least based on current block.timestamp), whereas the mutant only adds _lockTime to the stored unlockTime, so for small _lockTime values invoked later it can keep unlockTime unchanged or grow incorrectly — the test fuzzes _lockTime and demonstrates a case where reference increases unlockTime but mutant does not.

For any caller and any nonnegative lock delta, calling Put(lockDelta) on the correct contract sets the holder's unlockTime to at least block.timestamp (i.e. it will be >= block.timestamp when lockDelta>0) and specifically if lockDelta is large enough relative to now it increases unlockTime to >= block.timestamp+lockDelta; the mutant instead adds lockDelta to the stored unlockTime (acc.unlockTime+lockDelta) which can fail to reach block.timestamp+lockDelta for many inputs, violating that the resulting unlockTime is >= block.timestamp+lockDelta when the previous stored unlockTime is less than block.timestamp.

For any caller and any nonzero _lockTime, after Put(_lockTime) the correct contract guarantees the account's unlockTime is at least block.timestamp + _lockTime (i.e. it is updated using current time), whereas the mutant that adds _lockTime to the stored unlockTime can leave unlockTime < block.timestamp + _lockTime for some inputs and times, violating this rule.

For any caller and any non-negative _lockTime, after calling Put(_lockTime) the holder's unlockTime is at least block.timestamp (i.e. it never moves backwards) — the mutant that adds _lockTime to the stored unlockTime can make unlockTime remain stale and thus be < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any nonnegative _lockTime, after calling Put(_lockTime) the holder's stored unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (the reference updates using block.timestamp so unlockTime never stays below current time), whereas the mutant that adds _lockTime to the previous unlockTime can leave unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and times.

For any caller and any _lockTime and deposit amount, calling Put(_lockTime) on the correct contract sets the caller's unlockTime to at least block.timestamp + _lockTime (i.e., it never decreases below that extension), whereas the mutant resets/limits unlockTime to block.timestamp and thus can produce a smaller unlockTime for some inputs.

For any account that deposits with a positive _lockTime while its existing unlockTime is in the future, the reference contract ensures the resulting unlockTime is at least as large as the previous unlockTime (i.e., Put never decreases unlockTime when a caller supplies a positive _lockTime), whereas the mutant can decrease unlockTime to block.timestamp for such inputs.

For any caller and any _lockTime = 0, after calling Put(_lockTime) the caller's unlockTime in the reference is set to at least its previous value (i.e., Put with zero lock time never decreases unlockTime), but the mutant that assigns unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease a previously-future unlockTime to now and thus violates this.

For any actor and any deposit amount and lockTime, calling Put must not decrease the actor's unlockTime below its previous value when the previous unlockTime is in the future (the reference preserves a future unlockTime or extends it by block.timestamp+_lockTime), while the mutant that sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease a previously-future unlockTime to now and thus violates this rule for some inputs.

For any caller, calling Put(...) never decreases their unlockTime when their existing unlockTime is strictly in the future (reference preserves or increases it by comparing block.timestamp+_lockTime), but the mutant that assigns unlockTime = block.timestamp can reduce a future unlockTime to now for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any account and any deposit with lock delta L, the reference contract never decreases a holder's unlockTime when calling Put (it only updates unlockTime if the new computed time is greater), whereas the mutant unconditionally overwrites unlockTime to block.timestamp+L which can shorten (decrease) the unlockTime for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit with lock delta L, calling Put never decreases that caller's stored unlockTime (it only increases it if block.timestamp+L is greater); the mutant overwrites unlockTime unconditionally and can decrease it for some inputs.

For any caller and any inputs, calling Put(...) on the reference never decreases that caller's stored unlockTime (it only updates it when block.timestamp+_lockTime is greater); the mutant can decrease unlockTime by unconditionally setting it to block.timestamp+_lockTime.

For any caller and any sequence of deposits, calling Put(...) never reduces that caller's stored unlockTime (reference only updates unlockTime when the new time is greater); the mutant unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp + _lockTime and can therefore decrease unlockTime for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit amount and lock delta, after calling Put the reference contract never decreases that caller's stored unlockTime (i.e., acc.unlockTime after Put is >= the previous acc.unlockTime), whereas the mutant can decrease unlockTime by unconditionally overwriting it with block.timestamp + _lockTime.

After any Put by an account with arbitrary previous unlockTime and any _lockTime, the reference contract sets acc.unlockTime to max(previous unlockTime, block.timestamp + _lockTime), but the mutant instead increments acc.unlockTime by _lockTime which can produce a smaller unlockTime when previous unlockTime < block.timestamp (violating the max rule).

For any caller and any _lockTime and value sent, after Put the holder's unlockTime equals the greater of the previous unlockTime and (block.timestamp + _lockTime); the mutant that does acc.unlockTime += _lockTime can produce a smaller unlockTime when previous unlockTime < block.timestamp, violating this max rule.
